verses.text: A meditation by David, sung to the LORD about what Cush the Benjaminite said. LORD my God, I take refuge in you. Save me from everyone chasing me. Rescue me
before they tear me apart like a lion, ripping me to pieces with no one to save me.
LORD my God, if I’ve done what they say, if my hands are guilty,
if I’ve done harm to someone who was at peace with me or robbed someone who opposed me for no reason,
then let my enemy chase me down and catch me. Let him trample my life into the ground and leave my honor in the dust. Selah.
Rise up in anger, LORD. Stand against the fury of my enemies. Wake up and help me. You’ve called for judgment.
Let the assembled peoples gather around you. Rule over them from on high.
The LORD judges the peoples. Judge me, LORD, according to my righteousness and the integrity in me.
Put an end to the evil the wicked are doing, and give the righteous a firm footing. You are the righteous God who searches hearts and minds.
God is my shield. He saves people whose hearts are honest.
God is a righteous judge, a God who feels indignation every day.
If a person refuses to turn back, God sharpens his sword. He has already bent his bow and strung it.
He’s prepared his deadly weapons and made his flaming arrows ready.
Look at the one who labors to do evil. They conceive trouble and give birth to lies.
They dig a hole and fall into the very pit they made.
The trouble they cause comes back on their own head. Their violence lands on them.
I’ll thank the LORD for his righteousness and sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.
